chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abi Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Sawiq is the food of the sent messengers, or he said: the prophets.

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: A simple dish made of flour, often mixed with water or curds, associated with prophetic diet.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Al-Sawiq in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Al-Sawiq as the sustenance of the prophets, a narration that underscores the virtue of simplicity and humility in dietary habits within Shia tradition. This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, serves as a practical guideline for believers to emulate the ascetic lifestyle of the messengers by favoring modest, easily digestible foods over extravagance. The designation of this dish as 'food of the sent ones' elevates it from mere sustenance to a symbol of spiritual purity and prophetic continuity.
